answer: Use the ocm-channel facility: show ocm-channel-<name>/<lower-frequency>/<upper-frequency> [opm-pwr] [connected]. It lists the detected carriers within the configured OXcon(s). name is a String (length 0..64); lower-frequency and upper-frequency are uint32 and give the lower/upper frequency of the corresponding spectrum power (OPM-pwr point); opm-pwr is the Optical Parameter Monitor power in dBm, decimal64 range -99.00..99.00 with default -99; connected yields 'true' if the channel is configured, i.e. involved in an oxcon, values true/false with default false. ocm-channel is show-only and is available in Operational Mode and Candidate Configuration Mode.

Yes. On ocm-mp the ocm-enable attribute, which enables regular power monitoring, takes values disabled or enabled and defaults to enabled. Configure it with set ocm-mp-<name> [label <value>] [admin-state <value>] [ocm-enable <value>] - those three are the only settable attributes besides the name. The related read-only monitoring-state also defaults to enabled: the system reports 'enabled' when an OMS reference exists. Other show-only attributes include monitored-port (the port being monitored, can differ from supporting-port for a non-integrated OCM, default not-applicable) and ad-direction, which for ocm-mp only takes the value ingress. admin-state defaults to unlock and managed-by is system. Access: Operational and Candidate Configuration Mode.

The ocm-ptp facility is available for WS04S cards within a CD-AD ADG and provides dedicated OCM monitoring. It is not on by default: ocm-enable (enables regular power monitoring) takes enabled or disabled and defaults to disabled, so you must turn it on, for example set ocm-ptp-1-1.2-ocm1-in ocm-enable enabled. Settable attributes are label, admin-state (lock/unlock/maintenance, default unlock) and ocm-enable. Read-only: ad-direction (egress or ingress, default ingress), last-measurement (date-and-time or never, default never), adg-number (uint8, range 0..110, default 0), and monitoring-state, which defaults to disabled and reports 'enabled' only when complete connectivity at the AD is established and OCM measurement is possible.

On the oms facility, grid-mode defaults to flexible. Permitted values: flexible, fixed-50G-96ch, fixed-100G-48ch, fixed-75G-64ch, fixed-75G-64ch-oif, fixed-50G-7100 (88 channels, set automatically when osc-compatibility is osc-7100) and fixed-150G-40ch. Default spectrum limits are lower-frequency 191300000 and upper-frequency 196150000 (191.3 to 196.15 THz, standardC-band). monitoring-mode selects how the section is monitored: not-monitored (non-intrusive monitoring, no OCM/DGE required), intrusive (TTP), non-intrusive (CTP, operates with OCM e.g. DGE), dge-fixed-attenuation (fixed attenuation due to a connected interstage device), ila-with-equalization (operates with DGE and OCM) and integrated-equalization (integrated DGE). Default is intrusive for all node types except ILA, not-monitored for ILA, and integrated-equalization for hyperscale ILA nodes. It is only exposed for an OMS of a port that belongs to a degree, or on an ILA node.

set ops-<name> accepts label, admin-state, alarm-report-control, input-psd-profile, role and port-expansion. input-psd-profile is the nominal expected tributary channel power density in dBm/12.5GHz, decimal64 range -30..-6, default -6. role is one of tributary (single add/drop to a local or remote transponder), multi-carrier (multiple carriers on the underlying filter port), general-purpose (other cases, e.g. express cross-connection to another filter), ase-input (only on specific RD ports in SLTE l0-mode-op) and active-multi-carrier (multiple carriers with active port control); default is general-purpose. port-expansion is no or y-cable, default no, intended for Y-cable expansion. supported-roles is read-only and shows which roles the card, and sometimes the card-mode, allows. Example: set ops-1-6-ad1 role tributary.

On optical-carrier, frequency is the center frequency, range 0 | 191275000..196125000 MHz (0 means not configured), with the usable sub-range set by module and pluggable: CHM7 and CHM7X 190625000-196725000 MHz step 50 MHz, CHM6 191333000-196117000 MHz step 50 MHz, CHM2TX 191292500-196137500 MHz step 1 MHz, CHM1R with TOM-400G-C-DWDM 191275000-196125000 MHz with fine tune. tx-power is the transmit power into the fiber, range -55.0..55.00 dBm with accuracy adjustable in steps of 0.5 dBm and per-module limits, for example CHM2TX -6 to 0 (default 0), CHM7/CHM7X -10 to 0 (default -2), UTM2 default -6.0, CHM1R with TOM-400G-C-DWDM -10 to 1 (default 1). For a slight trim use frequency-offset, int16 range -6000..6000 MHz, default 0: once set, the frequency changes slowly over 1-10 s without affecting service.

Yes, with propagate-shutdown on the optical-carrier facility: when set, the transmit laser will be shut down if the whole service of that direction has signal failure. The function is mainly used in a regeneration node to propagate signal failure as LOS. Values are enabled and disabled, default disabled. The companion propagate-shutdown-holdoff-timer sets the hold off time of propagate shutdown, range 0..2000 milliseconds, default 0. Restriction: neither propagate-shutdown nor propagate-shutdown-holdoff-timer is configurable on the SPN2 or SPN2C card. Example form: set optical-carrier-1-1-1 propagate-shutdown enabled.

Very little. The only settable attributes are label and admin-state: set optical-channel-<name> [label <value>] [admin-state <value>]. label is a String of length 0..256; admin-state takes lock, unlock or maintenance and defaults to unlock. Everything else is read-only through show optical-channel-<name>: supporting-card, supporting-port, supporting-facilities, supported-facilities, AID, oper-state (enabled/disabled, default disabled), avail-state and managed-by (system or user, default system; only user-created facilities can be user deleted). Access is Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode. Example: set optical-channel-channel1 admin-state unlock.

Read laser-state on the optical-ptp facility: it reports the emitting pump (for example booster) laser state, values disabled or enabled, default disabled, and is show-only. It is only of relevance for DWDM line ports; on RD amplifiers it means the source (Tx) pump is disabled, on Raman modules it refers to the pump laser and the actual traffic emitted from the dwdm-line port. Yes, you can add fixed pad on receive: fix-rx-attenuation is a settable fixed attenuator before port Rx, decimal64 with 2 fraction digits, range 0..30 dB, default 0, where 0 dB means no fixed attenuator. Example: set -f optical-ptp-1-6-dwdm fix-rx-attenuation 10. The matching fix-tx-attenuation (0..30 dB, default 0) is only visible when ops.port-expansion=y-cable is configured. Measured powers appear in power-actual-rx and power-actual-tx (-99.00..99.00 dBm, default -99).

The Signal Fail decision uses working-los-threshold for the Working Path and protection-los-threshold for the Protection Path. Both are settable optical power in the range -55.0 to 0 dBm and default to -23 dBm. Signal Degrade uses working-switch-threshold and protection-switch-threshold, same -55.0 to 0 dBm range, default -18 dBm, and SD-based switching only happens when switch-threshold-enable is enabled (default disabled). facility-los-threshold sets the facility port threshold below which loss of signal is declared, range -55 to 15 dBm, default -30.0 dBm. Hysteresis is configurable: los-threshold-hysteresis (SF) defaults to 3 dB and switch-threshold-hysteresis (SD) to 2 dB, both range 0.5 to 5.0 dB in 0.1 dB steps, with 1 dB recommended for MCHP and OMSP deployments.

set osc-<name> accepts label, admin-state, alarm-report-control, l0-comm-interface-type, osc-control, target-output-power, tx-power-adjustment, voa-attenuation-target-rx and lof-soak-timer. osc-control is auto or manual, default auto; HSC OLS nodes only support auto. target-output-power is the OSC Tx power at the DWDM line port output, either na or a value in [-2.5..4.5] dBm, default na. tx-power-adjustment trims the automatically calculated Tx power target in osc-control auto mode, na or [-6..6] dB, default 0. voa-attenuation-target-rx is the target Rx VOA in manual control mode, [0..30] dB, default 10. l0-comm-interface-type is ipv4 or ipv6, ipv4 for standard OLS and ipv6 for SLTE and HSC OLS. lof-soak-timer is short (about 3 ms) or long (18,400 OC-3 frames, about 2300 ms), default short, applicable only to the PBAx card. Read-only: osc-mode, osc-wavelength, voa-attenuation-actual-rx, power-actual-rx/tx.

Read otdr-state on the otdr facility: show otdr-<name> otdr-state. Values are not-available (status not available), idle, measuring (measurement is ongoing), finished (measurement has completed) and fail (measurement has failed); default not-available, and a status change triggers a change notification. Supporting read-only attributes: otdr-measurement-time gives the time remaining in the current measurement (default 0), otdr-error carries the error message produced when the measurement ends with error, otdr-laser-state shows the laser as not-available/enabled/disabled, otdr-measurement-port gives the port under measurement (0 means the card is not measuring any port), otdr-measurement-direction is not-available/tx/rx, and otdr-ongoing-measurement-profile shows none, short, medium, long, or raman-precheck1/2/3. Example: show otdr.

On otdr-ptp: otdr-range sets the distance range used to calculate the measurement repetition period, auto or [0...300.0 km], default auto; set it to the fiber length plus 10 percent. From R9.1, if the OTS can be traced through the fiber connection between the ILA/ROADM card and OTDR8OFP2, auto is derived from OTS fiber-length-tx/fiber-length-rx with 10 percent margin rounded up to the nearest 10 km. otdr-resolution is the data sampling resolution, auto or [0.4...100.0], default auto. otdr-pulse-width is auto or [10...20,000 ns], default auto. otdr-measurement-speed is fast (about 10 s), medium (about 15 s), slow (about 1 minute), precision (3 to 5 minutes), high-precision (5 to 7 minutes) or auto, default auto. otdr-ior is auto or [1.0...2.0]. peak-power is auto or [5...14.5]. launching-fiber-length is [0...50 m], default 0, and auto is not supported.

On the ots facility. Fiber type: fiber-type-tx and fiber-type-rx, both default SSMF, chosen from AllWave, DrakaLL, DSF, LEAF, LS, PSLC, PureSilica, SMF-ULL, SSMF, Teralight, TWC, TWMinus, TWPlus, TWReach, TWRS, VistaCor (rx also allows not-applicable, auto and not-configured). Length: fiber-length-tx and fiber-length-rx, auto or [0..500.0] km, default auto, required for tilt control and for Raman backward pumping. Loss: span-loss-transmit and span-loss-receive, decimal64 2 fraction digits, range 0..80 dB (rx also 99 dB), default 0; 0 and 99 dB count as not configured for rx and changing span-loss-receive is traffic affecting. Extra loss such as patch panels goes in external-attenuation-tx/external-attenuation-rx, 0..30 dB, default 0. span-loss-reference (configured or measured, default measured) selects which source power control uses; span-loss-aging-margin-rx is 0.00..10.00 dB, default 1.0.

The ots-diagnostics name is auto generated by the system on line card provisioning. The format is 'ots-diagnostics-<chassis>-<slot>-<DWDM Line>', for example show ots-diagnostics-1-1-dwdm-line for an RD20TM DWDM line terminating an OTS section, or ots-diagnostics-1-1-dwdm-line1 and ots-diagnostics-1-1-dwdm-line2 for C2ILASGH which terminates two lines. Only nmoper-alarm-reporting (disabled/enabled, default disabled; when enabled a mismatch between expected-operator and rx-operator raises the NMOPER alarm) and expected-operator (up to 32 characters) are settable. tx-operator is also defaulted by the system, with format '<ne-name>-<Dxx>', default <ne-name>-D00. tti-style, rx-operator and tti-port-id are read-only.

On ots-r, required-fiber-type-rx defaults to SSMF. It is the required fiber type on the DWDM Line for the Rx fiber and is only of relevance if control-mode = auto and there is no fiber-connection; the choices are AllWave, DrakaLL, DSF, LEAF, LS, PSLC, PureSilica, SMF-ULL, SSMF, Teralight, TWC, TWMinus, TWPlus, TWReach, TWRS and VistaCor. Other settable receive-span attributes: fiber-length-rx (unspecified or 0..500.0, default unspecified), span-loss-receive (the span loss at the receiving dwdm-line, default 99), external-attenuation-rx (user configured external attenuation), delta-pointloss (additional Rx attenuation determined after turning up pumps, e.g. a bad splice at dwdm-line Rx: not-applicable or -1..3.5 dB, default not-applicable), plus label, admin-state and alarm-report-control. Read-only: configured-fiber-type-rx, configured-fiber-length-rx, span-loss-at-amplifier, power-actual-rx and connected-reference.

Yes, and it does depend on that. The automatic-otdr attribute on ots-r-auto-otdr enables or disables OTDR based automatic fiber check; values enabled and disabled, with default enabled for green field deployments and disabled for in-field SW upgrade. If the Raman card is associated with a base card equipped with integrated OTDR the default is enabled; if the NE has a Raman card that is not aggregated with the EDFA card the value is disabled. The setting persists over warm/cold restart and over SW upgrade. Disabling it while a test is running aborts the ongoing OTDR test and releases the amplifier that the automatic OTDR had blocked; disabling with no test running means no further tests are triggered until re-enabled. Progress is shown by auto-otdr-state: not-applicable, not-available, pass, in-progress, fail, aborted. loss-calibration-by-otdr is none (green field), rx-only, tx-only or tx-rx, default none. Example: set ots-r-auto-otdr-1-1-dwdm-line automatic-otdr enabled.

Use add oxcon-<name> source <value> destination <value> [label] [activation-mode] [auto-delete] [activation-request-fwd] [activation-request-bwd] [direction] [target-output-power-src] [target-output-power-dst] [circuit-id], with the two media channels as source and destination, for example: add oxcon-1-80-192262500__1-3.1-dwdm-line-192262500 source 'nmc-1-80-192262500' destination 'nmc-1-3.1-dwdm-line-192262500'. direction is two-way or one-way, default two-way. Whether it comes up by itself depends on activation-mode: automatic means the service is activated automatically by the system on creation and deactivated automatically on deletion, and it is the default in the standard L0 mode of operation; manual (default in SLTE mode) and activate-on-create (default in HSC OLS mode) require activation-request-fwd/bwd set to activate. target-output-power-src and target-output-power-dst range -18.00..15.00 dBm, defaulting to 0 dBm in most cases and -5 dBm for Add/Drop OXcons between a Tributary NMC and an RD20TM/RD09SM NMC.

profile-control applies only to RD20TM operating in card-mode = slte or slte-backhaul, and it runs in Operational Mode only. Syntax: profile-control [type=]<value> [entity=]<value> [direction=]<value> [[profile-data=]<value>]. type is write-attenuation-profile, read-attenuation-profile, create-power-profile, read-power-profile or read-ocm-power; entity is the instance the profile applies to (for example oms-1-8-dwdm-line or nmc-RD20-1-1); direction is tx or rx, but for power-profile only tx is supported. Note that for RD20TM in card-mode = slte the power profile and OCM power are defined at the output of the booster, before the EVOA, not at the DWDM line out port. OMS attenuation values run 0 to 25.50 with N = 776 slices for standardC-band at 6.25 GHz; NMC attenuation values run -10 to 25.50 with N not exceeding 32.

Not much: set pump-<name> only accepts label, admin-state and alarm-report-control. label is a String of length 0..256, admin-state takes lock, unlock or maintenance, and alarm-report-control is allowed or inhibited with default Allowed. Everything else on the pump facility is read-only through show pump-<name>: supporting-card, supporting-port, supporting-facilities, supported-facilities, AID, oper-state (enabled/disabled), avail-state (in-service, out-of-service, normal, abnormal, low-power), managed-by (system or user, only user-created facilities can be user deleted) and pump-type. To change the actual Raman pump power use the separate pump-power command and its target-pump-power attribute. Access mode is Operational and Candidate Configuration mode.

Use set pump-power-<name>/<pump-id> target-pump-power <value>, where pump-id is the integer identifying the pump. target-pump-power is the Raman pump power in dBm, applicable when control-mode is manual, values -99.00..99.00 dBm or not-applicable (default not-applicable), with 0 used for the not-applicable case; on an RPBM card the target-pump-power must be in the range 12 to 30 dBm. If the value is outside the operating range of the Raman sled, the alarm PUMP-Fail (STAT FAIL PSTAT) is raised. The permitted ceiling and floor are readable: show pump-power-<name>/<pump-id> min-target-pump-power max-target-pump-power, both decimal64 with 2 fraction digits over -99.00..99.00 dBm or not-applicable. configured-pump-power shows the power configured in hardware (derived automatically when control-mode is auto, otherwise from target-pump-power) and actual-pump-power shows what is currently measured, default -99.

Read calibration-state on the raman-calibration facility: show raman-calibration-<name> calibration-state. It displays the state of the automatic Raman gain calibration process, with values not-available (calibration has not been triggered or no prior calibration has occurred), in-progress (currently running), up-to-date (completed successfully and current), out-dated (stale due to OTS OLOS, a change in delta pointloss, etc.) and fail (ended with a failure); default is not-available. last-calibration-timestamp gives when the last calibration rpc completed, with or without errors (date-and-time, or never). When the state is fail or out-dated, additional-info (string up to 1024 characters) carries troubleshooting information. Also available: gain-calibration-error (residual gain error in dB after each iteration), calibrated-delta-pointloss (suggested delta-pointloss, -3..3.5 dB) and intermediate-results. Example: show raman-calibration-1-8.

rsc is the Raman card Pilot Tone facility. Syntax: set rsc-<name> [label <value>] [admin-state <value>] [alarm-report-control <value>] and show rsc-<name> [supporting-card] [supporting-port] [supporting-facilities] [supported-facilities] [AID] [label] [admin-state] [oper-state] [avail-state] [managed-by] [alarm-report-control] [rsc-power-rx] [rsc-power-tx]. What it reports is the pilot tone power: rsc-power-rx is the received Pilot Tone integrated power and rsc-power-tx is the transmitted Pilot Tone integrated power, both show-only. admin-state takes Unlock, Locked, Maintenance or Unknown, default Unlocked; alarm-report-control is Allowed or Inhibited, default Allowed; oper-state is enabled or disabled with default enabled; managed-by defaults to system. Access: Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode.

Because the server-layer OMS is not in a monitoring mode that creates it. The spectrum facility is only instantiated by the system when the underlying server layer OMS monitoring-mode is configured either as non-intrusive or ila-with-equalization; the spectrum object is only of relevance if the DGE2 is intended to be used in the NE, and the existence of the managed object depends on the OMS monitoring-mode. Set the OMS monitoring-mode accordingly and the spectrum object appears. Related read-only attribute dge-in-use reports true if the corresponding OMS monitoring-mode is ila-with-equalization, default false. On spectrum you can then set label, admin-state, alarm-report-control and attenuation-setting, a single attenuation value for the entire spectrum, range 0..30 dB, default 0 dB, editable only when attenuation-control-mode = manual and control-mode = auto-max-pw.

Use the spectrum-control object, keyed by name, direction and slice center frequency: add or set spectrum-control-<name>/<direction>/<center-frequency> [attenuation-target <value>] [target-output-power <value>]. direction is ingress or egress, but currently only egress is supported and egress is the default; center-frequency is the band slice center frequency in MHz and is managed by the system. attenuation-target is the required attenuation for that spectra, range [0..30] dB, default 0, and is only possible to configure when a Dynamic Gain Equalizer, or equivalent, is in use (dge-in-use = 'true'). target-output-power is the intended target output power for the spectra, not-specified or [-55..55] dBm, default not-specified. show adds width (detected width in MHz, 0 if the frequency does not match or no ILAx card or DGE is fiber-connected) and attenuation-actual. Example: set spectrum-control-1-7-dwdm-line2/egress/194943750 attenuation-target 1.
